npmPublishPolicy.summary: npm publish is a developer-driven, pre-merge manual step run via scripts/publish-npm.sh. npm forbids re-publishing or deleting an existing version number, so a defect discovered after publish is never fixed in place: the package is bumped to the next version and the whole publish+confirm procedure re-run.
npmPublishPolicy.confirmationProbe: npm view <name>@<version> resolves (polled up to 60s), then a scratch-dir npm install <name>@<version> + import() succeeds (plus --help for packages with a bin).

issues.title: plgg-bundle を npm から入れると、2 回目の起動で relocate の symlink を消せず EISDIR で落ちる

rootCause.commitTitle: Remove plgg-bundle relocate.mjs, run from dist
rootCause.summary: relocate.mjs's rmSync(symlinked node_modules, {force:true}) step was deleted; a registry install now imports dist/cli.es.js directly with no /tmp relink, so the EISDIR code path no longer exists.

issues.reproEnvironment: macOS, Node v23.9.0 per the issue body. The one live-registry run so far (PR #214) used Linux/Node 22.23.4 and did NOT reproduce the symptom even against the still-published 0.0.6 — a green Linux run is not sufficient evidence this issue is closed; the repro needs the Node version named in the issue, or an equivalent that throws EISDIR for rmSync on a directory symlink.
issues.residualGap: None in source; only missing a regression test pinning the already-fixed behavior and the version bump to actually ship it.

implementingPRs.role: duplicate 0.0.7 bump + own gate; superseded by #212, recommend closing without merge

consumerGate.state: OPEN, opt-in (network-dependent), not yet exercised against a merged/published fix

publicEvidenceToClose.check: repeat build in a clean consumer, on a Node version that reproduces EISDIR pre-fix
publicEvidenceToClose.command: npm pack plgg-bundle@0.0.7 into a scratch dir consumer, then `npx plgg-bundle` twice in the same directory (see #212 scripts/bundle-repeat-build.spec.mjs or #213 scripts/gate-corpd-consumer.mjs)

publicEvidenceToClose.expect: packages[name=plgg-bundle].version == 0.0.7 and checks[id=bundle-restart].status == passed, captured on a Node version in the affected range
publicEvidenceToClose.status: pending — last run (2026-10-25T09:44:33Z, Linux/Node 22.23.4) still shows version 0.0.6 and did not reproduce the bug on this Node version either way

blockers: #189 (the #156 declaration-path fix, same package) is not yet rebased into the same branch as #212 — publishing 0.0.7 before both tracks land means a second bump (0.0.8) is required to add the other later, since npm forbids re-publishing 0.0.7
npm publish itself is a developer-driven manual step; no sandbox agent holds npm publish credentials
issues.closeCondition: plgg-bundle@0.0.7 (containing #212's bundle-repeat-build.spec.mjs coverage) is live on the npm registry per `npm view`, and a clean npm consumer on a Node version that reproduces the original EISDIR runs `npx plgg-bundle` twice in the same directory with the second run exiting 0.

rollback.trigger: The post-publish Confirmation step in .workaholic/deployments/npm.md fails (registry doesn't resolve within the poll window, or the scratch install/import/repeat-build check fails).
rollback.action: Do not merge the PR that staged the failed version. Bump packages/plgg-bundle/package.json to 0.0.8, fix whatever the Confirmation check caught, and re-run the full procedure from `PREFLIGHT=1 ./scripts/publish-npm.sh`.
rollback.irreversibility: npm forbids deleting or re-publishing an existing version number, so 0.0.7 can never be corrected in place once published broken — only superseded by a later version.

issues.title: plgg-bundle を npm から入れると、利用側の TypeScript 7 を掴んで transpile できない

rootCause.note: Commit 5b109cec removed the relocate.mjs symlink step that caused the app-build transpile path to resolve the consumer's top-level TypeScript, so the issue's literal `target: "app"` repro no longer occurs on main. But declaration (.d.ts) emission in packages/plgg-bundle/src/domain/usecase/emitDts.ts independently resolved `typescript` by walking up from the package's own root, which does not reliably prefer the package's nested typescript@6 over a consumer's top-level typescript@7 in every layout. That residual gap is still open on main.

issues.residualGap: emitDts.ts's ad hoc typescript resolution, fixed only in PR #189's new vendors/consumerCompiler.ts.

implementingPRs.role: source fix (consumerCompiler.ts, used by emitDts.ts and nodeProc.ts)
test-only: packs plgg-bundle, installs into an isolated TypeScript 7 fixture consumer, asserts the app build works
carries the shared 0.0.6->0.0.7 bump this issue also needs
duplicate 0.0.7 bump; superseded by #212, recommend closing without merge

consumerGate.state: OPEN, opt-in; #214's one-off run of the same scenario (check id consumer-ts7) failed against the currently-published 0.0.6 with a CommonJS error, matching this issue

publicEvidenceToClose.command: isolated consumer with typescript@7.0.2 at the top level and plgg-bundle's own nested typescript@6 dependency, `npx plgg-bundle` with target:"app" (see #179 scripts/gate-bundle-ts7-consumer.ts or #213/#214 check id consumer-ts7)
publicEvidenceToClose.expect: build succeeds, no TranspileError / 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading CommonJS)'
emitted .d.ts resolves plgg-bundle's own nested typescript, not the consumer's top-level one

publicEvidenceToClose.command: n/a — verified on the qmu/corpd side, not in this repository
publicEvidenceToClose.expect: corpd's top-level typescript returns to a single `typescript@7` dependency instead of aliasing tsgo + pinning typescript@6.0.3
publicEvidenceToClose.status: pending, out of this repo's scope

blockers: #189 and #179 are not yet combined with #212's 0.0.7 bump in one branch — publishing 0.0.7 from #212 alone, without #189's fix, would require an 0.0.8 bump later to add it, since npm forbids re-publishing 0.0.7
issues.closeCondition: plgg-bundle@0.0.7 (containing #189's consumerCompiler fix) is live on npm per `npm view`, an isolated TypeScript 7 consumer fixture builds the app and emits declarations without resolving the consumer's own typescript, and corpd's config drops the tsgo alias workaround.

rollback.trigger: Same shared-version Confirmation step as issue #155 (plgg-bundle@0.0.7 is one publish for both issues).
rollback.action: Same as issue #155: bump to 0.0.8, fix, re-run the full publish procedure. Do not publish 0.0.7 a second time.

issues.title: plgg-view：dispatch の描画をフレームでまとめ、変わらない部分木を飛ばす lazy が欲しい

rootCause.note: The fix exists only on unmerged PR #166; nothing frame-batches dispatch or implements lazy() on main.

implementingPRs.role: source fix: batches application's dispatch->view->diff into one animation frame (render:"sync" selectable for tests), adds lazy(fn, arg) to skip view/diff when the argument is referentially unchanged; bumps plgg-view 0.0.2->0.0.3

issues.conflictNote: PR #216 (opened 2026-10-25T09:55:28Z, after #166) also bumps plgg-view to 0.0.3 while fixing issue #158, and its own body states #166 'must be rebased/versioned after this release to avoid a version collision.' Only one of #166/#216 can ship as plgg-view@0.0.3 — see issue #158's conflictNote for the same pair.

consumerGate.state: OPEN, opt-in; #214's one-off run shows checks id frame-dispatch and lazy-subtree both failing against the currently-published 0.0.2, matching this issue

publicEvidenceToClose.command: mount an application, fire several dispatches within one animation-frame tick, count view()/diff invocations (see #166's own render.spec.ts, or #213/#214 check id frame-dispatch)
publicEvidenceToClose.expect: exactly one view+diff pass per animation frame regardless of how many dispatches landed in it

publicEvidenceToClose.command: wrap a subtree in lazy(fn, arg), re-render with an unchanged arg reference (check id lazy-subtree)
publicEvidenceToClose.expect: fn is not called again and no diff walks that subtree

blockers: Version collision with #216 (see conflictNote) — whichever of #166/#216 merges second must rebase onto the other's 0.0.3 bump rather than republish the same version
issues.closeCondition: plgg-view@0.0.3 (containing #166's frame batching and lazy()) is live on npm per `npm view`, and corpd observes exactly one render per animation frame across several same-frame dispatches, with lazy-wrapped subtrees skipping view/diff.

rollback.trigger: Post-publish Confirmation step fails for plgg-view@0.0.3, or the version collision with #216 is discovered only after one of the two has already published 0.0.3.
rollback.action: Do not merge the losing PR as-is. Rebase it onto the other's already-published 0.0.3 content, bump to 0.0.4, and re-run the full publish procedure.
rollback.irreversibility: npm forbids re-publishing 0.0.3 under different content, so whichever of #166/#216 ships 0.0.3 second must carry a new version number, not a corrected 0.0.3.
